subject: Proposed proportional SLO offset for April latency spike
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novablend.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike on 2028-04-09 — request for SLO assessment

Hi Laura,

We observed a sustained latency increase from ~09:30–16:55 PDT yesterday (region: us-west-2) that affected our inference throughput and caused a backlog in our batch pipeline. Our internal monitoring shows an estimated 12,000,000 tokens processed during the window with average p95 latency up ~6x. We rely on Redwood for real-time features, so this materially impacted end-user experience.

Can you confirm whether this qualifies as an SLO breach and, if so, what the process is for determining a service offset/credit? Wed like a rough estimate of the amount and timeline — we have a renewal coming up and want to understand the financial impact. Ive attached our exported request logs and a short summary of the user impact.

Attachments:
- novablend_incident_window.log (3.2MB, text)
- novablend-impact-summary.pdf (summary)

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Ops Lead, Novablend Inc.
elena.torres@novablend.com
+1 (415) 555-0132
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novablend.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike on 2028-04-09 — request for SLO assessment

Hi Elena,

Thank you for the report and the logs — Ive received them and started an internal validation. Apologies for the disruption.

Next steps from our side:
- Well validate the event window against our observability (routing, kernel fallbacks, and autoscaler activity).
- If we confirm an SLO breach, finance and sales will compute the proportional offset and issue a credit against the April invoice.
- Ive CCd Marissa (sales) and Evelyn (billing) so we can queue the credit calculation.

Could you confirm the monthly invoice amount for March/April billing we should reference for proportional calculation? If you prefer, we can do a token-proportional credit instead.

I will follow up within 48 hours with an eligibility assessment and a preliminary credit figure.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: calc proposal — Novablend April 9 event

LAURA / EVELYN — internal calc proposal after reviewing the logs and our telemetry:

Summary facts we confirmed:
- Region: us-west-2 (single region routing)
- Incident window (customer-observed): 2028-04-09 09:30–16:55 PDT (7.42 hours)
- Tokens during window (customer-provided): 12,000,000 tokens
- Monthly invoice referenced by customer: $124,500 (Novablend confirmed)
- Redwood SLO: 99.95% monthly availability (per contract)

Calculation approach (proportional, per SLA sec 3.2):
1) Convert SLO allowance to hours/month: 0.05% of 720 hours = 0.36 hours (21.6 minutes).
2) Actual outage/degradation: 7.42 hours.
3) Multiple of allowed downtime = 7.42 / 0.36 = 20.6x.
4) SLA matrix: for 1x-10x => 5% credit, 10x-25x => 10% credit, >25x => 20% (cap 30% per monthly invoice). Given 20.6x, falls in 10x-25x tier.

Proposed credit = 10% of monthly invoice = 0.10 * $124,500 = $12,450.
Alternative (token-proportional): tokens impacted / monthly tokens * monthly bill. We dont have customer monthly token volume; customer supplied window token count only.

Attachments: slo_credit_calc-20280411.xlsx (breakdown with minute-level telemetry + working math).

Recommendation: approve 10% credit for this incident and issue as an invoice adjustment/credit note applied to next billing cycle. If legal or customer wants a higher remediation path, escalate to policy exceptions with Finance.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novablend.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike on 2028-04-09 — request for SLO assessment

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the logs and for the patience while we validated. Weve completed the eligibility assessment and calculation. Summary below:

What we confirmed
- Incident window: 2028-04-09 09:30–16:55 PDT (7.42 hours)
- This exceeded the contracted SLO allowance (99.95% monthly) by a factor of ~20.6x.

Approved offset
- Per the SLA matrix (section 3.2), this event falls in the 10x-25x tier. We have approved a credit equal to 10% of your monthly invoice.
- Monthly invoice used for calculation: $124,500.
- Credit amount: $12,450.

Next steps
- We will issue a credit note for $12,450 applied to your next Redwood invoice. That will be visible on your account within 3 business days.
- Ive attached the calculation workbook and a short acknowledgement template for your records.
- If you prefer a token-proportional adjustment instead of a dollar percentage, let us know and we can run that alternate calculation.

Attachments:
- slo_credit_calc-20280411.xlsx (detailed math)
- customer_ack_template.txt (acknowledgement form)

If this works, reply with a quick confirmation and well proceed to issue the credit.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
